'''''Persoonia cornifolia''''' is a plant in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Proteaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to eastern Australia. It is a shrub with elliptic to egg-shaped leaves and hairy yellow flowers, and grows in northern [[New South Wales]] and south-eastern [[Queensland]].

==Description==
''Persoonia cornifolia'' is an erect or spreading shrub with hairy young growth. The leaves are elliptic to egg-shaped, {{cvt|20–80|mm}} long, {{cvt|10–45|mm}} wide and flat with the edges more or less turned downwards. The leaves are hairy when young but become [[wikt:glabrous|glabrous]] with age. The flowers are arranged in small groups in leaf [[wikt:axil|axil]]s with a scale leaf at the base of each flower. Each flower is on the end of a densely hairy [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] {{cvt|1–2|mm}} long. The flower is composed of four hairy [[tepal]]s {{cvt|10–13|mm}} long, which are fused at the base but with the tips rolled back. The central [[Style (botany)|style]] is surrounded by four yellow [[Stamen#anther|anthers]] that are also joined at the base with the tips rolled back, so that it resembles a cross when viewed end-on. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is usually hairy. Flowering occurs from December to February and is followed by fruit which are green [[drupe]]s.<ref name="RBGS">{{cite web|last1=Weston|first1=Peter|title=''Persoonia cornifolia''|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&lvl=sp&name=Persoonia~cornifolia|publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref><ref name="RBGS(2)">{{cite web|last1=Weston|first1=Peter|title=''Persoonia''|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/NSWfl.pl?page=nswfl&showsyn=&dist=&constat=&lvl=gn&name=Persoonia|publisher=Royal Botanic Garden Sydney|access-date=20 December 2017}}</ref>

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Persoonia cornifolia'' was first formally described in 1830 by [[Robert Brown (botanist, born 1773)|Robert Brown]] from an unpublished manuscript by [[Allan Cunningham (botanist)|Allan Cunningham]]. Brown's description was published in ''[[Supplementum primum Prodromi florae Novae Hollandiae]]''.<ref name="APNI">{{APNI | name = ''Persoonia cornifolia'' A.Cunn. ex R.Br.| id = 58592}}</ref><ref name="R.Br.">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Robert|title=Supplementum primum prodromi florae Novae Hollandiae:|date=1830|location=London|page=16|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/77294#page/530/mode/1up|access-date=19 December 2017}}</ref>

The [[Botanical nomenclature|specific epithet]] (''cornifolia'') is derived from the [[Latin]] words ''cornu'' meaning "horn"<ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.}}</ref>{{rp|421}} and ''folium'' meaning "leaf".<ref name="RWB" />{{rp|340}}

==Distribution and habitat==
This persoonia grows in woodland and forest north from the [[Moonbi Range]] in north-eastern New South Wales and in south-eastern Queensland.<ref name="RBGS" /><ref name="ala">{{cite web|title=''Persoonia cornifolia''|url=http://bie.ala.org.au/species/http://id.biodiversity.org.au/node/apni/2916492|publisher=Atlas of Living Australia|access-date=20 December 2017}}</ref>
